short: AV-HuBERT's masked audio-visual cluster pre-training (M03) was a large step past distillation, but its LRS3 gains lack repeated runs and later work beats it at matched budgets.
position: The paper [@shi2022avhubert] changes two components: the pre-training objective (M03), masked prediction of audio-visual cluster labels refined iteratively, and audio as training-only supervision (M02), with video alone at test. The M03 gain over the paper's own scratch baseline is large (92.3% to 32.5% WER at 30 h of labels, 62.3% to 28.6% at 433 h), but that baseline is weak: a supervised conformer in Table 1 reaches 43.3% at 433 h, so the 33.7-point gain overstates the gain over a tuned system, and the margin over distillation [@afouras2020asr] mixes data, model and decoder (inference). Both components remain standard: one test set, no repeated runs (Table 1). Later work beats the design at matched budgets: 23.7% against 32.5% at 30 h, and 21.5% against 26.9% at 433 h even after this paper's self-training [@haliassos2026usr2] [later]. The 1/1000-of-the-labels headline rests on a 1.1-point gap (32.5% against 33.6% [@makino2019rnnt], no variance); the firmer result is the self-trained 26.9% at 433 h, 6.7 points lower (inference).
